title: Global-scale, verifiable mineral storage of carbon dioxide

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a repeatable way to store large quantities of carbon dioxide underground by converting it into solid minerals in reactive rock, while verifying how much conversion actually occurs. Success would require dependable performance across a range of geological settings, extending beyond favorable individual sites. Mineralization is already an active technology; the missing advance is globally deployable, verifiable performance.

Conceptual synthesis: The capability combines finding suitable reactive rock, bringing CO₂ into contact with it, sustaining fluid movement as minerals form, managing underground pressure and measuring the resulting carbon storage. Injection totals alone cannot establish the amount mineralized. Verification must distinguish carbon delivered underground from carbon shown to have become solid minerals, while accounting for carbon whose fate remains uncertain.

significance.text: Conditional significance: Reliable mineralization across many geological settings could substantially broaden access to durable geological carbon storage. The revolutionary step would be making storage performance predictable and repeatable across locations, with evidence that permits others to audit the amount stored. That would give storage planning a stronger basis than extrapolating from a small number of favorable demonstrations.

This advance would directly address the storage component of carbon management. Capturing CO₂, transporting it to a suitable site and reducing emissions remain separate requirements. Whether a particular project achieves net carbon removal would depend on where its CO₂ comes from and the emissions associated with its full operation. Successful underground mineralization alone would not establish net removal.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more locations able to host durable storage and more defensible carbon accounting for projects that use it. Those possibilities depend on acceptable water requirements, costs, operating reliability and environmental risks. Demonstrating rapid conversion at one site would not by itself establish climate-scale capacity, low costs or suitability in other rock formations.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is sustained, verifiable mineralization at large scale across diverse geological settings. The supplied research identifies a central engineering tension: reactive rock must remain accessible to CO₂-bearing fluids even as mineral precipitation can reduce the permeability needed to reach more rock. An operational breakthrough must sustain useful contact and flow over time, rather than merely demonstrate that a rock can react.

Water demand, injectivity and pressure management are additional barriers identified in the supplied research. A useful system would need to avoid impractical freshwater requirements while maintaining injection performance and controlling leakage and seismic risks. The supplied review did not have retained source text with which to establish the magnitude or severity of these constraints, so their site-specific importance and acceptable operating limits remain open.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: Verification must connect observations from a limited set of wells and monitored flow paths to a defensible carbon balance for the storage operation. It must separate measured quantities, tracer-based inferences and extrapolations, and quantify uncertainty in carbon that has not been located or characterized. Geological characterization, geochemistry, hydrology and reservoir engineering must therefore work together with carbon accounting.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes an important pilot result to the 2024 review, “Carbon Mineralization in Fractured Mafic and Ultramafic Rocks”: tracer-based analysis at CarbFix1 inferred that more than 95% of the injected dissolved CO₂ mineralized along the monitored flow path within two years. This is a reported inference with a defined monitoring scope, rather than a direct measurement of every part of the reservoir. The supplied material does not establish equivalent conversion throughout an entire storage formation or across other sites.

The research also reports that the same review describes larger cumulative injection at CarbFix2. No injection quantity, operating interval or corresponding mineralized fraction is supplied here. Larger cumulative injection and verified mineral conversion are different achievements; the former cannot establish the latter without additional evidence. Neither the reported CarbFix1 inference nor the CarbFix2 injection history establishes globally repeatable, low-cost mineralization at climate-relevant scale.

These findings must be read with an evidence-access limitation. The supplied source index contains the review’s title and DOI but no retained document, extracted text or other source artifact. The accompanying assessment therefore could not inspect the cited sections 2.2.3–2.2.4 or Figure 2, confirm the quantitative claims, or assess document completeness. The research notes a 2024 correction to the article, but its content and effect are not supplied. These limitations leave the reported findings unverified within this record; they do not demonstrate that the findings are false.

Temporal limitation: No bounded search record or later evidence was supplied, so this record cannot assess developments through November 1, 2026. The two-year figure describes the reported pilot’s conversion interval; it does not date the experiment. The available material supports describing a reported pilot achievement and subsequent injection activity, with unresolved questions about scale, transferability and practical performance.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Independently monitored sites in different rock types and geological settings should sustain substantial mineralization over an explicitly defined operating period. A convincing program would specify in advance what counts as large scale, how long performance must persist and what constitutes successful replication. These would be proposed evaluation thresholds, not established standards. A finite collection of successful sites would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested settings, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained mineralization replicates across independently monitored, geologically diverse sites

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification: Each site should provide an auditable carbon mass balance that distinguishes injected carbon, carbon inferred or measured to be mineralized, other stored carbon and unresolved quantities. Monitoring methods, assumptions, uncertainty estimates and the spatial reach of observations should be available for independent scrutiny. Replication should test whether the measurement and inference methods remain reliable under different flow conditions and geological structures.
completion_criteria.label: Auditable site carbon mass balances quantify mineralization and uncertainty

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: Demonstrations should report lifecycle emissions, water use and water source, costs, injection performance, pressure management, leakage observations and seismic monitoring. Acceptance limits should be declared and justified for the intended application. Sustained performance should show whether mineral precipitation progressively restricts access to reactive rock and whether maintaining operation remains practical.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained operational practicality is assessed against justified acceptance limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation: Completion should include a clear account of where the method works, where it fails and which conditions control that boundary. Evidence for durable mineral storage should be assessed separately from claims about capture, transport or net carbon removal. Broader deployment claims would require capacity and resource assessments beyond successful site demonstrations.
completion_criteria.label: Mineral storage applicability, failures and controlling conditions are documented

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: GEO-03, “Geothermal reservoirs engineered economically in ordinary deep rock,” has the closest engineering overlap through subsurface access, permeability, fluid circulation and pressure management. Its objective is useful heat extraction; GEO-04 aims to convert and retain carbon in minerals. Mineral precipitation may constrain fluid access in GEO-04, making its reaction and flow requirements distinct from those of an engineered geothermal reservoir.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-01, “Reliable short-term forecasting of damaging earthquakes,” and GEO-10, “Reliable transferable forecasting of volcanic eruptions,” share questions about interpreting subsurface observations and establishing predictive reliability across sites. Seismic risk management is relevant to GEO-04, but reliable storage does not require solving general earthquake or eruption forecasting. Their forecasting objectives remain separate from storage verification.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-06, “Discovery of globally consequential recoverable geological hydrogen,” overlaps in geological resource characterization and the need to establish practical performance beyond a promising occurrence. It concerns finding and recovering an energy resource; GEO-04 concerns placing carbon underground and verifying its conversion and retention. Neither capability establishes the other.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-02, “A chemically and thermally resolved map of Earth’s deep interior,” GEO-05, “Recovery of a detailed geological record of Earth’s first half-billion years,” GEO-07, “Reconstructing the Moon-forming impact from independent geological evidence,” and GEO-08, “Establishing when and how sustained plate tectonics began,” share an interest in geological composition, reactions or inference from incomplete observations. Their targets are deep-Earth structure and planetary history; GEO-04 requires operational characterization and monitoring of particular storage formations.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-09, “Predictive laws linking erosion, sediment transport and landscape evolution,” shares the ambition to develop explanations that transfer across settings. Its focus is surface processes and landscape change, whereas GEO-04 concerns subsurface reactive flow and carbon storage. Transferability is a common scientific challenge, not evidence that either innovation subsumes the other.

unresolved_issues: The source document and cited passages were not retained, so the CarbFix1 quantitative inference and its precise observational scope remain unverified within the supplied evidence.
The CarbFix2 cumulative injection quantity, operating dates and independently supported mineralized fraction are not supplied.
The content of the article’s reported 2024 correction and whether it affects any relevant claim remain unknown.
The site-specific magnitude of permeability loss, water requirements, leakage risk and seismic risk cannot be established from the supplied source metadata.
Operational definitions of large scale, sustained duration, acceptable cost, resource use and risk remain to be specified.
No supplied search record establishes developments through November 1, 2026; this record cannot determine the latest state of deployment.

brief.title: Reliable carbon storage in rock around the world
possible: More places could store carbon dioxide underground by turning it into solid minerals, a process called mineralization. Storage operators could predict how well it would work in different rocks and provide measurements that others could audit.
why: Repeatable results across different geological settings would give communities and storage planners a stronger basis for choosing sites. Clear accounting would let projects claim storage based on how much carbon became mineral, rather than simply how much they pumped underground.

sources.showed: This review examines underground carbon mineralization in reactive rocks, including the CarbFix demonstrations.
sources.cited_for: It supports the case that rapid mineralization has occurred at a pilot site.
sources.not_established: A favorable pilot does not establish predictable conversion across different geological settings.

sources.showed: At CarbFix2, the team inferred substantial mineralization. The well’s injectivity, its ability to accept fluid, stayed stable, indicating unchanged permeability, the rock’s ability to let fluid through.
sources.quote:
Notably, the injectivity of the injection well has remained stable throughout the study period conﬁrming that the host rock
permeability has been essentially unaﬀected by 3.5 years of mineralization reactions.
sources.cited_for: It supports sustained mineralization and fluid flow at an operating storage site.
sources.not_established: This geothermal site does not establish comparable performance, costs or water needs elsewhere.

sources.who: B. P. McGrail and colleagues at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
sources.showed: Wallula rock samples contained ankerite, a mineral containing carbon, linked chemically to the injected gas. X-ray diffraction, a test that identifies minerals, confirmed its identity.
sources.quote:
Characterization by x-ray diffraction identified these nodular precipitates 
as ankerite, the identical iron and calcium rich carbonate observed to form in laboratory tests with Columbia River 
basalts.
sources.cited_for: It provides physical evidence that injected carbon became mineral in another field setting.
sources.not_established: Finding minerals in samples does not establish how much of the total injected carbon became solid.

sources.who: Mohammad Nooraiepour, Mohammad Masoudi, and Helge Hellevang
sources.showed: This preprint found that slower seawater flow enabled visible mineral formation in laboratory tests. It also identified connections between pores, the rock’s tiny spaces, that could clog.
sources.quote:
Post-experiment analyses identified calcium carbonate and smectite
phases.
sources.cited_for: It supports the importance of fluid contact time and connected pores for mineral formation and continued flow.
sources.not_established: Laboratory results do not establish sustained seawater-based storage in an underground formation.

shown: At CarbFix2 in Iceland, Clark and collaborators calculated that over 60% of injected carbon became mineral during the higher injection phase. The well continued accepting fluid without a sustained decline. This demonstrates sustained operation in a particular geothermal setting.

At Wallula in Washington, McGrail and colleagues found minerals containing carbon chemically linked to the injected gas. Together, these trials establish that underground mineral formation works in the field.
missing: Large-scale mineralization has yet to sustain comparable performance across independently monitored, diverse geological settings.
Whole-site carbon accounting must distinguish mineralized carbon, other stored carbon and carbon whose fate remains uncertain.
Long-term operation must maintain fluid flow while meeting justified limits for water use, costs, emissions, pressure, leakage and earthquake risk.

milestones.label: Sustained mineralization across diverse, independently monitored sites
milestones.explanation: Independently monitored sites in different geological settings would have to sustain substantial mineralization over a defined period. This would establish repeatability across the settings tested.

milestones.label: Auditable accounting of stored carbon and uncertainty
milestones.explanation: Each site would have to account for injected carbon, mineralized carbon, other stored carbon and unresolved amounts, with uncertainties open to scrutiny. This would make storage claims independently assessable.

milestones.label: Sustained operation within justified practical limits
milestones.explanation: Demonstrations would have to meet justified limits for emissions, water, costs, injection, pressure, leakage and earthquake risk while minerals form. This would establish whether continued operation remains practical.

milestones.label: Clear boundaries between suitable and unsuitable storage settings
milestones.explanation: Results would have to explain where storage works, where it fails and which conditions control success. This would define its reach while assessing mineral storage separately from capture, transport and net carbon removal.

uncertain: How large, long-lasting and affordable must a demonstration be to count as success?
How reliably can observations from a few wells establish mineral conversion throughout a storage formation?
How strongly will growing minerals restrict fluid flow, and can seawater reduce freshwater demand without undermining conversion?

page.title: In situ carbon mineralization at commercial injection rates
page.definition: Projects in basalt and peridotite inject more than 1 million metric tonnes of CO₂ per year into underground rock, where reactions form solid carbonate minerals. Independent verification quantifies the mineralized mass and uncertainty separately from dissolved, free-phase and unresolved carbon.

goal.need: IEAGHG's 2025 inventory reports a worldwide injected total smaller than one year at its illustrative commercial injection rate. Its recommendations call for testing monitoring methods at that scale.

figures.caption: Injection quantities reported by IEAGHG
figures.note: The quantities have different time bases. Neither measures mineralized mass.

statements.quote: further demonstrations nearing commercial scale and across different reservoir geologies are likely needed to develop regulatory frameworks.

statements.body: U.S. Department of Energy, Carbon Transport and Storage Program
statements.quote: ensure modeling and monitoring tools can accurately represent fluid, chemical and petrophysical dynamics in an in situ CO2 mineralization storage project.
statements.context: The programme identifies this as the goal of its mineralization modeling and monitoring research.

completion.title: Commercial injection in basalt and peridotite yields independently verified mineral storage.
completion.criterion: For each host-rock case, a permitted project injects more than 1 million metric tonnes of CO₂ during one year. An independent verification body verifies a site-wide carbon balance that quantifies mineralized CO₂ and its uncertainty, distinguishes dissolved and free-phase CO₂, accounts for leakage and identifies unresolved carbon. Operation complies with the site's permit. The numerical benchmark concerns injection; the verified result must state the mineralized mass separately.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas, combining a published injection-scale example with mineralization verification requirements and demonstration in both host-rock cases.
completion.basis: IEAGHG's 2025 review, DOE's 2024 programme, Isometric's in-situ module and Carbfix's deployment targets were searched; no combined cross-rock completion test was found. This Atlas synthesis uses IEAGHG's illustrative commercial injection scale and protocol-based mineralization accounting in basalt and peridotite. It establishes demonstrated breadth in those cases, without establishing universal geological applicability.

milestones.title: Laboratory experiments demonstrate carbonate formation in a CO₂–water–rock system.
milestones.criterion: Laboratory measurements physically validate a predicted mineral-forming reaction under DOE's generic TRL 3 criterion. Basalt: a preprint submitted on 2 January 2026 reports calcium carbonate in a calcite-buffered basaltic-glass column at 80 °C and 0.005 mL/min over 30 days; it is not peer reviewed and does not establish net storage. Peridotite: Section 3 of the 2024 review describes laboratory carbonation studies of olivine-rich rocks. These examples are not formal DOE readiness assessments.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, Technology Readiness Assessment Guide, TRL 3; a generic experimental proof-of-concept criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: laboratory-scale studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology.

milestones.title: Reservoir cores demonstrate carbonate minerals formed from injected CO₂.
milestones.criterion: Reservoir cores contain newly formed carbonate minerals attributable to injected CO₂. Basalt: Wallula injected nearly 1,000 metric tonnes in July and August 2013; post-injection cores contained ankerite identified by X-ray diffraction and isotopic attribution. Peridotite: on 5 November 2024, 44.01 reported mineralizing 10 tonnes in Fujairah in under 100 days; this announcement is not peer reviewed and does not establish the core-based test.
milestones.set_by: Isometric, in-situ mineralization module v1.2, Section 3.3; core studies are an accepted verification method.
milestones.threshold_quote: Core studies to verify mineralization within the reservoir

milestones.title: A field injection yields a quantified mineralized fraction and conversion timescale.
milestones.criterion: Reactive and non-reactive tracers distinguish mineral trapping from fluid mixing and quantify its fraction and timescale. Isometric specifies no fixed conversion percentage. Basalt: CarbFix1 inferred >95% mineralization along the injection-to-monitoring flow path within 2 years. CarbFix2 injected 23,200 metric tonnes of CO₂ from June 2014 through December 2017; its higher-injection phase inferred >60% mineralization within 4 months, with stable well injectivity over the 3.5-year study.
milestones.set_by: Isometric, in-situ mineralization module v1.2, Section 3.1.3.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: quantify the percentage and rate or timescale of trapping and the amount of potential leaks.

milestones.title: A mineral-storage project obtains a geological-storage operating permit.
milestones.criterion: The competent authority authorizes CO₂ injection and storage in the selected reservoir, subject to site-specific operating and monitoring conditions. Basalt: Iceland's Environment and Energy Agency issued the Hellisheiði decision on 30 April 2025, allowing up to 106,000 metric tonnes of CO₂ annually and 3,180,000 tonnes over 30 years. These are authorized quantities, not demonstrated storage.
milestones.set_by: Iceland's Environment and Energy Agency, Hellisheiði permit decision; this decision concerns basalt. Isometric requires an applicable CO₂ injection permit for either host-rock case.
milestones.threshold_quote: Með þessu starfsleyfi er veitt heimild til niðurdælingar koldíoxíðs í jörðu til geymslu

milestones.title: A mineral-storage project injects more than 1 million metric tonnes of CO₂ in one year.
milestones.criterion: Actual annual injection exceeds 1 million metric tonnes, IEAGHG's illustrative commercial-scale benchmark. Basalt: Coda Terminal's published full-scale target is 3 million tonnes annually. Peridotite: Frontier's announcement on 15 October 2026 identifies continuous operation over multiple years as the next demonstration. Neither announcement establishes achievement of this injection test.
milestones.set_by: IEA Greenhouse Gas R&D Programme, 2025 review, monitoring recommendations; an illustrative scale example, not a mandatory industry cutoff.

not_found: The 2025 paper Rapid mineralisation of carbon dioxide in peridotites and its Southampton and Oxford repository copies could not be opened.
The OSTI copy of the Wallula paper could not be opened; its abstract was accessible through Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
No independently verified site-wide mineralized-carbon balance at more than 1 million metric tonnes of annual injection was found for either host-rock case.

results.finding: CarbFix2 monitoring of 76 fluid samples inferred over 60% of injected CO₂ mineralized within four months.
results.detail: The estimate compared dissolved inorganic carbon with a non-reactive mixing prediction. For the higher-injection phase, tracer concentrations were extrapolated from earlier measurements, assuming unchanged flow paths.
results.quote:
Using the same approach, when the amount of
injected gas was doubled in July 2016, we calculate that
over 60% of injected CO 2 and over 85% of injected H 2S
were mineralized within four months after the gas-
charged waters were continuously injected into CarbFix2
site.

results.finding: Wallula post-injection cores contained ankerite attributed to 977 metric tons of injected CO₂.
results.detail: X-ray diffraction identified ankerite; its isotopic signature aligned with the injected CO₂. The paper reports 50 sidewall cores collected.
results.quote:
Laboratory 
analysis of discrete carbonate nodules removed from post -injection side-wall cores were identified as being ankerite, 
and contained isotopic signatures closely aligned with isotopic composition of the CO 2.

results.finding: Wallula observed carbonate formation within 24 months of CO₂ injection.
results.detail: The study provides qualitative evidence of mineralization but does not quantify a mineralized fraction using reactive and non-reactive tracers.
results.quote:
Consequently, the isotopic 
composition data coupled with groundwater chemistry data and geophysical wellbore surveys conclusively show that 
injected supercritical CO2 was being actively converted to a stable carbonate mineral in the basalt reservoir within 24 
months of emplacement.

results.finding: Wallula received a state permit for CO₂ injection limited to 1,000 metric tons.
results.detail: The paper reports an injection permit but does not establish the permit's storage authorization or site-specific monitoring conditions.
results.quote:
An extended -duration pumping test conducted in the Fall of 2011 resolved  
uncertainty over hydrologic connectivity to shallower basalts  ( i.e. potential for leakage) and injection zone 
heterogeneity, thus enabling a State permit to be issued to conduct a CO 2 injection limited to a maximum 1,000 MT.

results.finding: Wallula injected 977 metric tons of CO₂ over three weeks in 2013.
results.detail: The reported injection is below the benchmark of more than 1 million metric tonnes in one year.
results.quote:
Over a course of three weeks in July -August of 2013, CO 2 was injected into the Columbia 
River basalt at a rate of ~40 MT/day for a total volume of 977 MT.

results.finding: Basaltic-glass column experiments produced calcium carbonate over 30 days; the number of successful columns was not reported.
results.detail: CO₂-acidified seawater flowed through a calcite-buffered column at 80°C and 0.005 mL/min. The experiment does not establish net CO₂ storage.
results.quote:
Post-experiment analyses identified calcium carbonate and smectite
phases.

results.finding: In 15 fractured basalt cores, carbonate formation was observed as early as 6 weeks.
results.detail: Three batches of five cores were exposed to CO₂-equilibrated water. Raman spectroscopy identified siderite; model predictions of its distribution and carbonate volume were consistent with observations. This was not a formal DOE readiness assessment.
results.quote:
Carbonation in basalt fractures was observed as early as 6 weeks, with Mg-
and Ca-bearing siderite formed in both basalts reacted at 100 °C and Mg-Fe-Ca carbonate minerals formed in the
ﬂood basalt reacted at 150 °C.

results.finding: One partially serpentinised dunite core formed an XRD-confirmed magnesite coating less than 1 mm thick.
results.detail: The core was exposed to wet supercritical CO₂ for 246 days at 70°C and 100 bar. The modeled solution was undersaturated with respect to magnesite despite its observed formation; the authors discuss possible causes for the discrepancy.

results.finding: Carbfix’s Hellisheiði basalt storage project (1 permit) was authorized to store up to 106,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year.
results.detail: The permit, dated 30 April 2025, authorizes a total of 3,180,000 tonnes over 30 years and requires site-specific monitoring. These are authorized quantities, not demonstrated storage.
results.quote:
Rekstraraðila er heimilt að taka á móti og geyma í jarðlögum allt að 106.000 t/CO 2 á ári, samtals 
3.180.000 t/CO2 yfir 30 ára tímabil, á geymslusvæði sem staðsett er að jarðhitasvæðinu á Hellisheiði

results.finding: Silverstone, one project: more than 19,000 tonnes of CO₂ injected in one year.
results.detail: The reported period was 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. The stated lower bound does not establish that annual injection exceeded 1 million tonnes.
results.quote: During the period, more than 19,000 tonnes of CO₂ were injected through older geothermal wells that are now used for reinjection.

results.finding: Carbfix reports more than 120,000 tonnes of CO₂ mineralized at Hellisheiði since the method was first implemented.
results.detail: The source also claims mineralization within two years, but does not report tracer measurements or a quantified mineralized fraction for this result.
results.quote: Since the Carbfix method was first implemented at Hellisheiði, a total of more than 120,000 tonnes of CO₂ and more than 50,000 tonnes of H₂S have been permanently mineralized in rock.

results.finding: Paraná basalt experiment (one column; replicates not specified): carbonate precipitate contained 75.95% aragonite.
results.detail: CO₂-charged water passed through basalt grains at 25 °C. FTIR and XRD characterized precipitate collected in the solution reservoir; glass wool contributed quartz to the sample. This was not a formal DOE readiness assessment.
results.quote:
Therefore, the CO
2
capture experiment yielded a precipitate comprising 75.95% aragonite, 19.34% dolomite, and 4.60% calcite mineral assemblage.

results.finding: One 15 g serpentinized peridotite sample formed approximately 46% magnesite in the post-carbonation material.
results.detail: The CO₂–water–rock batch experiment ran for 96 hours at 185 °C and 100 bar. X-ray diffraction identified magnesite; the study is not a formal DOE readiness assessment.
results.quote:
Instead, approximately 46 % magnesite was formed in the post- 
carbonation material.
